abstract: Let $F$ be a squarefree quintic and let $S_F$ be the K3 surface $Y^2=X^3+F(s)^2$. For very general $F$ its Kuga–Satake variety is isogenous to a product of powers of an elliptic curve $E_K$ with multiplication by $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$, of $\operatorname{Jac}(C_F)$ for $C_F:v^3=F(s)$, and of one abelian sixfold. We prove that the full Clifford Kuga–Satake correspondence $v\mapsto(a\mapsto vav_0)$ of $S_F$ is algebraic for every $F$. The family satisfies the fixed-curve hypothesis of Bolognesi–Laterveer's published Kuga–Satake statement; our contribution is an independent explicit construction of the specified map, following the Gaussian quotient and specialization strategy of rStation paper 32. The known half-twist construction supplies one block of this map. The second block comes from a symmetric-square quotient of $C_F\times C_F\times E_K$, which is birational to a uniruled Weierstrass threefold over $\mathbb P^2$ branched along the six tangent lines to a conic. A quaternion-algebra multiplicity argument shows that these two blocks and their adjoints generate the whole map. Combined with Varesco's ordinary Hodge conjecture for powers of these surfaces and the full-spin criterion of rStation paper 36, this gives the generalized Hodge conjecture for $S_F^r\times\operatorname{KS}(S_F)^n$, and for every power of $B\times E_K$ whenever $B$ is a polarized abelian fourfold with $K$-action whose rational Hermitian datum is that of the family. We explain why the same method stops at $K$-dimension four.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: Attribution and description changes requested by the v1 review; no change to any proof or result. (1) Section 1: the Bolognesi-Laterveer sentence now states that X->zeta X fixes X=0, Y=+-F(s) and the zero section, so S_F satisfies their fixed-curve hypothesis and Theorem A lies within their announced scope. (2) New paragraph 'Methodological precedents' in Section 1 citing paper 32 v3 [16, Sections 10.2-10.3, 10.7-10.8] and paper 59 [15]; one-sentence pointers to [16] in the proof of Proposition 3.2 and at the start of Section 5; reference [16] added; abstract novelty sentence updated accordingly. (3) Supplement: six_point_repair_check.py no longer prints that canonical singularities are certified; its output file and MANIFEST.json hashes are regenerated. No other supplement file changed.

coauthors.contribution: Section 5 (specialization of the specified flat Clifford class, written by the second author); independent derivation of the symmetric-square quotient; the rational rank-one division-module explanation in Lemma 4.2; the pull-push support transfer replacing a resolution analysis; the period-plus-Zarhin route in Proposition 4.1; independent proof of the low-rank overlap (Lemma 7.1, including the n=1,2 cases); the twelve-point middle-block observation of Section 7.2; independent rerun of the finite checks; adversarial audit of the full text.
